mainText: Good morning. Here is your curated AI briefing for Sunday, October 25, 2026. Recent economic analysis suggests that artificial intelligence has yet to provide a measurable financial benefit to most large corporations. Torsten Slok, chief economist at Apollo Global Management, examined the S&P 500 while excluding major technology firms—Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia, and Tesla—to evaluate the impact of AI on the broader economy. His findings indicate that profit margins and revenue per worker have remained flat for these companies, suggesting that widespread AI investment has not yet translated into improved corporate productivity. Slok argues that while AI functions effectively as a calculator, it lacks the human capacity for judgment, trust, and accountability required to drive actual business growth. This report aligns with other recent studies that have similarly struggled to identify significant productivity gains across the corporate sector. In infrastructure news, Bayer Crop Science has detailed the development of its Agentic Decision Engine, a system designed to streamline complex plant breeding decisions. Previously, Bayer’s researchers struggled with a fragmented operational process that required manual navigation through various logs, dashboards, and metadata stores to understand machine learning results. The new system, built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, utilizes a multi-agent architecture where a supervisor agent routes queries to specialist agents. These agents retrieve context from relevant data sources without requiring the user to navigate the underlying technical stack. Bayer reports that the system currently resolves approximately 80 percent of user questions without manual engineering intervention. Additionally, OpenAI and Poland’s NASK National Research Institute have entered into a partnership aimed at advancing artificial intelligence safety and security. The collaboration will focus on evaluating the capabilities of frontier AI models, identifying potential vulnerabilities, and establishing technical safeguards. This initiative builds on existing cooperation between OpenAI and Polish cyber defenders; earlier this year, experts at CERT Polska used OpenAI models to identify six security flaws in MikroTik RouterOS, all of which the vendor has since addressed. OpenAI stated that such international partnerships are vital for creating standardized approaches to AI risk assessment and ensuring that global safety efforts remain aligned with the practical realities of how the technology is deployed. In the developer ecosystem, Hugging Face has released a tool to help users determine which models are compatible with AWS Trainium hardware. The new model support Space allows developers to query popular models to see if they run on Trainium instances, provides the necessary scripts for execution, and lists specific compilation requirements. Separately, Microsoft and Hugging Face have collaborated on a project called ThinkingBox. This tool evaluates AI agents by verifying the actual state of a database after a task is completed, rather than relying on the agent’s own claims of success. By using these database outcomes as a reward signal during training, the researchers were able to improve the repeatability of performance in a model tasked with corporate workflows. The consumer market continues to see an influx of AI-powered wearable devices. New gadgets range from productivity-focused pendants like Limitless, which records and summarizes meetings, to more experimental hardware like the Friend pendant, which is designed to act as an emotional support companion. Amazon has also expanded its wearable lineup, introducing the Bee Frontier and Bee Eclipse devices, which are designed to learn user routines and create reminders. Meanwhile, Meta has announced its Muse personal AI assistant, which is expected to ship in a pocket-sized device featuring a digital avatar named Jolly. Looking ahead, industry observers will be monitoring how non-tech companies reconcile the high costs of AI implementation with the current lack of quantifiable financial returns noted by market analysts. Additionally, the continued expansion of agentic systems in enterprise environments, such as the deployment seen at Bayer, may provide further data on whether these tools can reliably automate complex decision-making processes in regulated industries. That is your curated AI briefing for today.
